title: Exercise 15.3: Continuity and Discontinuity
notes: **Checklist.** At x = a verify that f(a) is defined, that lim(x→a) f(x) exists, and that the limit equals f(a); one failed condition identifies the discontinuity type.
**Finding a parameter.** Equate LHL and RHL at the boundary: if f(x) = kx + 1 for x ≤ 2 and 3x − 1 for x > 2, then 2k + 1 = 5 gives k = 2.
**Classifying breaks.** Equal finite one-sided limits with f(a) wrong or missing is removable; unequal finite limits is a jump; an unbounded one-sided limit is infinite.
**Worked example.** f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2) has a removable discontinuity at 2 because both one-sided limits equal 4 while f(2) is undefined.
**Domain endpoints.** At the left endpoint use only the right-hand limit, and at the right endpoint only the left-hand limit, when asserting continuity on a closed interval.
**Exam caution.** State which condition fails; 'discontinuous' alone does not distinguish a hole from a jump and loses method marks.
summary: Exercise 15.3 tests continuity and discontinuity: verify all three conditions, classify the break, and solve for parameters at piecewise boundaries.
